page.text:
A *subgroup* $H \leq G$ is a subset of a group that is itself a group
under the inherited operation. To qualify as a subgroup, $H$ must be
nonempty, closed under the group operation ($x * y \in H$), and closed
under inverses ($x^{-1} \in H$).

By the *One-Step Subgroup Test*, a nonempty subset $H \subseteq G$ is a
subgroup if and only if for all $x, y \in H$, the product
$x * y^{-1} \in H$. Subgroups form the atomic building blocks of group
theory: every group contains the trivial subgroup $\{e\}$ and the
improper subgroup $G$, while the intersection of any family of subgroups
is again a subgroup.
